Mental Health Care Plan

- Tertiary: Decreased libido since job change (likely stress-related)

Formulation
Predisposing: Pre-existing hyperthyroidism; high-pressure profession  
Precipitating: Recent job change leading to increased workload and perceived stress  
Perpetuating: Ongoing high work demands, extensive screen time, limited coping strategies documented  
Protective: Seeking medical help; denies substance misuse; no risk behaviors identified

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Occupational stress/anxiety
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce headache frequency and severity  
  • Feel calmer at work and improve overall wellbeing
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Clarify contribution of anxiety vs. thyroid dysfunction to somatic symptoms  
  • Provide stress-management support and/or psychological therapy
- Actions (Patient):
  • Book and attend in-person GP appointment for examination and labs  
  • Monitor stress triggers; note frequency of headaches/palpitations
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Perform physical exam; order thyroid function tests and other relevant labs  
  • Screen for anxiety/depression (e.g., GAD-7, PHQ-9) at next visit  
  • Provide brief psychoeducation on stress management; consider referral for CBT or psychologist  
  • Review results and adjust thyroid medication if indicated

Secondary Problem: Reduced appetite and weight loss
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Restore normal appetite and weight stability
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Determine whether weight change is stress-related, endocrine-related, or both
- Actions (Patient):
  • Keep simple food diary; aim for regular balanced meals
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Assess nutritional status; consider dietitian referral if ongoing  
  • Re-evaluate weight and appetite at follow-up

Tertiary Problem: Decreased libido
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Improve sexual wellbeing
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Explore psychosocial vs. endocrine contributors
- Actions (Patient):
  • Discuss concerns openly with partner if comfortable
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Include libido inquiry in review after thyroid results and stress management interventions

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Not recorded
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating headaches, persistent palpitations, further weight loss, emerging low mood
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded (to be discussed at next visit)

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: To be set at next in-person appointment (recommend within 4–6 weeks)

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mental health diagnosis, structured risk assessment, sleep data, detailed MSE, documented goals/consent/education, follow-up date  
● Internal conflicts: DOB unclear—patient states age 35 but verbalizes “nineteen ninety-three something” (would make age ~30)  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio generally clear; DOB segment indistinct (“ninety , three something”)
